ctene.e: From the stem of Ancient Greek κτείς (kteís, “comb”).

s.d: a locomotor organ consisting of a row of strong cilia whose bases are fused
A band of fused cilia on the bodies of ctenophores, used for locomotion.

ctenidium.e: Borrowed from Medieval Greek κτενίδιον (ktenídion, “comb”). By surface analysis, cteno- + -idium.

s.d: comb-like respiratory structure serving as the gill of certain mollusks
A respiratory system, in the form of a comb, in some molluscs
A row of spines in some insects
resembling a comb; having projections like the teeth of a comb
Having a toothed margin, usually fish scales

ctenophore.e: Borrowed from translingual Ctenophora; equivalent to cteno- + -phore.

s.d: biradially symmetrical hermaphroditic solitary marine animals resembling jellyfishes having for locomotion eight rows of cilia arranged like teeth in a comb
Any of various marine animals of the phylum Ctenophora, having lucent, mucilaginous bodies bearing eight rows of comblike cilia used for swimming.
x: Ctenophores are abundant in the oceans, but long-neglected by scientists.
